# Owen Ford

## Overview

- **Age:** 30 to 35 years old  <sub>[v4 c23 P4](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0004)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c22 P15](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0015)</sub>
- **Status:** Engaged to Leslie Moore  <sub>[v4 c36 P0](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0000), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010)</sub>
- **Origin:** Ontario, Canada  <sub>[v4 c22 P15](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0015)</sub>
- **Role:** Newspaper man and author  <sub>[v4 c22 P15](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0015), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>

## Appearance

Owen Ford is a tall, broad-shouldered, exceptionally handsome man with a finely-cut nose and chin, large, brilliant dark-gray eyes, and a white, friendly smile. His thick brown hair is worn rather long, and his eyes give him an expression that is at times sad and absent. He dresses very well and possesses remarkably nicely shaped ears.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P4](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0004), [v4 c23 P9](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0009), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024)_

## Personality

Owen is an articulate, witty, and charming conversationalist with a delightful smile. He possesses a deep artistic soul, a love for nature, and a great capacity for earnest, passionate love. Though honorable and deeply moral in his actions, he is capable of intense, turbulent emotions when under emotional strain.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P4](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0004), [v4 c25 P13](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0013), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P11](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0011), [v4 c38 P7](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0007)_

## History

Owen Ford was born in Ontario, the son of Alice Selwyn and grandson of John Selwyn, the first schoolmaster of Glen St. Mary who built the little house of dreams. After working for years as a journalist and magazine writer, he suffered a severe bout of typhoid fever and was ordered to the seaside by his doctor to recuperate. In August, he went to Four Winds, boarders' accommodations having been arranged for him by Miss Cornelia Bryant at the home of Leslie Moore. Upon his arrival, Owen was struck by Leslie's extraordinary beauty, and soon fell deeply in love with her. Learning that her husband, Dick Moore, was hopelessly brain-damaged, Owen hid his feelings and poured his creative energies into writing a novel based on the 'life-book' of Captain Jim Boyd. After completing the manuscript in late summer, Owen confessed his agonizing, secret love for Leslie to Anne Blythe, before departing for Toronto without revealing his feelings to Leslie herself. Later, after Gilbert Blythe's medical intervention restored the memory of the man believed to be Dick Moore—revealing him to be his cousin, George Moore—Leslie became a free woman. Upon learning the news, Owen returned to Four Winds the following summer. He proposed to Leslie in Anne's garden, and they became engaged to be married in December. He also purchased the little house of dreams from the church trustees to serve as their summer home.

- Grandson of John Selwyn, the old Glen St. Mary schoolmaster, and his bride, Persis Leigh  <sub>[v4 c22 P15](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0015), [v4 c24 P22](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0022)</sub>

> And if inspiration comes from beauty, I should certainly be able to begin my great Canadian novel here.  <sub>[v4 c23 P19](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0019)</sub>

> We'll collaborate. You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we'll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim.  <sub>[v4 c25 P4](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0004)</sub>

> Mrs. Blythe, I love Leslie. LOVE her! That seems too weak a word!  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>

> It's burning, searing pain to love her and leave her—but not to have loved her is unthinkable.  <sub>[v4 c26 P18](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0018)</sub>
